clues: This city is in north Argentina. It sits on a big river, far north-west of Buenos Aires.
Winters are cool and dry here. Summers turn wet and warm, and the rain adds up each year.
Spain's settlers built this town first. No town in the land that is now Argentina came before it.
A lot of folks here still speak Quechua. It was the tongue of the Incas, and this is its last stop in the south.
This city is the mother of cities in this land. It is also the cradle of folklore here.
